questions.stem: Who did Addison raise the money for?

explain.定位:
A 9-year-old girl in New Mexico has raised more than $500 for her little brother who needs
heart surgery in Houston, Texas this July.
新墨西哥州一名9岁女孩为她需要在今年7月去得克萨斯州休斯顿做心脏手术的小弟弟筹得了
500多美元。
explain.信号:
首句 for 直接点出受益人。新闻头一句往往就是核心事实。这里 raised more than $500
for her little brother 中的介词 for 是答案信号——for 后面跟的人就是"为谁筹钱"的答
案，后面紧跟的 who needs heart surgery 又佐证了弟弟正是需要帮助的那个人。
explain.替换:
for her little brother ↔ Her little brother.
近乎原词，但锁定靠 for 这个信号
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 she overheard her grandfather and me talking 确实念到了 grandfather，但他
是在"商量怎么凑钱"的人，不是钱要给的人。听到 grandfather 就选 A，正是落进了"听到
原词就选"的陷阱。
借用原文：she overheard her grandfather and me talking
B) 张冠李戴
祖母 Kim Allred 是整段新闻的讲话人 said Allred，是"说事"的人，不是"被帮助"的人。把

借用原文：said Allred
C) 原词陷阱
her friends Erika and Emily Borden decided to sell lemonade 说明 Erika 是和 Addison
一起摆摊卖东西的伙伴，是"帮着筹"的人，不是钱要给的人。选项盗用了真出现的人名
Erika 来诱选。
借用原文：her friends Erika and Emily Borden decided to sell lemonade

options: A) By taking pictures for passers-by.
B) By selling lemonade and pictures.
C) By working part time at a hospital.
D) By asking for help on social media.

explain.定位:
She decided to go outside and have a lemonade stand and make some drawings and pictures
and sell them. That's when Addison and her friends Erika and Emily Borden decided to sell
lemonade for 50 cents a cup and sell pictures for 25 cents each.
她决定到外面摆一个柠檬水摊，画一些画，然后把它们卖掉。就在那时，Addison 和她的朋
友 Erika、Emily Borden 决定以每杯50美分卖柠檬水、以每张25美分卖画。
explain.信号:
并列动作 sell...and sell... 列全做法。答案信号是连续的动作动词与并列连词 and：sell
lemonade for 50 cents a cup and sell pictures for 25 cents each，两个 sell 把"卖柠檬
水"和"卖画"两件事都摆出来，这正是"怎么筹钱"的完整答案。
explain.替换:
sell lemonade for 50 cents a cup and sell pictures for 25 cents each ↔
By selling lemonade and pictures.
详述被概括：两个 sell 合并为 selling...and...
make some drawings and pictures and sell them ↔ selling lemonade and pictures
drawings and pictures 即 selling pictures 的来源
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音是 make drawings and pictures and sell them(画画并卖画)，选项 By taking
pictures for passers-by. 把它换成"给路人拍照"。picture 这个词录音确实念了，但配的动
作是"卖"不是"拍"，听到 picture 就选 A 即中招。
借用原文：make some drawings and pictures and sell them
C) 未提及
By working part time at a hospital. 里的 hospital 像是和"心脏手术"沾边，其实录音只提
到弟弟要做手术，从没说 Addison 去医院兼职打工筹钱，这一做法纯属虚构。
D) 原词陷阱
录音确实出现 The family turned to social media expressing their gratitude，但用社交
媒体是为了"表达感谢"，不是筹钱办法。选项 By asking for help on social media. 盗用
social media 一词并把用途偷换成"求助筹钱"。
借用原文：The family turned to social media expressing their gratitude

questions.stem: What was France's purpose of constructing the Ward Way?
options: A) Testing the efficiency of the new solar panel.
B) Providing clean energy to five million people.
C) Generating electric power for passing vehicles.
D) Finding cheaper ways of highway construction.

explain.定位:
Last week, France announced that the country will pave 621 miles of road with solar
panels over the next five years, with the goal of providing cheap, renewable energy to five
million people.
上周，法国宣布将在未来五年内用太阳能板铺设 621 英里道路，目标是为五百万人提供廉
价、可再生的能源。
explain.信号:
with the goal of 直接领出目的。答案信号是 with the goal of 这个短语——它明明白白
领出"目的"，紧跟其后的 providing cheap, renewable energy to five million people 就
是法国修路要达到的目标，正是本题答案落点。
explain.替换:
providing cheap, renewable energy to five million people ↔
Providing clean energy to five million people.
renewable energy 换成 clean energy
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 借了录音里反复出现的 solar panels 制造耳熟感，但录音从没说目的是"测试新板子的效
率"——"testing efficiency"原文根本没提，是听到 solar panel 就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：developing solar panels
C) 偷换概念
录音说供能给 five million people（人），C 却说 Generating electric power for passing
vehicles.（给过往车辆供电）。electric power 听着像 energy，但"给谁"被从"人"偷换
成"车"，录音通篇没提给车辆供电。
借用原文：providing cheap, renewable energy to five million people
D) 答非所问
录音后文确实提到 making them relatively cheap and easy to install，D 抓住 cheap 一
词说目的是"找更便宜的修路法"。但"便宜"是这套板子安装上的附带优点，不是法国修
Ward Way 的目的；目的句明写的是供能给五百万人。
借用原文：making them relatively cheap and easy to install

questions.stem: What is special about the solar panels used in the Ward Way?
options: A) They are made from cheap materials.
B) They are only about half an inch thick.
C) They can be laid right on top of existing highways.
D) They can stand the wear and tear of natural elements.

explain.定位:
The panels are also designed so that they can be installed directly on top of the existing
roadways, making them relatively cheap and easy to install.
这些板子还经过特别设计，可以直接安装在现有路面之上，使其安装相对便宜又简便。
explain.信号:
are designed so that 引出独特设计。答案信号是 are also designed so that——"经过
专门设计以便……"这类强调设计意图的句式，正是在点出板子的特别之处；其后 installed
directly on top of the existing roadways 即本题要的特点。文末 this is the first time a
panel has been designed to be laid directly on top of existing roads 又用"首次"再次
强化了这一点。
explain.替换:
installed directly on top of the existing roadways ↔
They can be laid right on top of existing highways.
installed≈laid、roadways≈highways
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音说的是安装"relatively cheap"，A 却说 They are made from cheap materials.（由廉
价材料制成）。cheap 一词录音真念过，但说的是"安装便宜"而非"材料便宜"，材料是否廉
价原文根本没提。
借用原文：relatively cheap and easy to install
B) 与原文相反
录音明说板子 only about a quarter of an inch thick（约四分之一英寸厚），B 却写 only
about half an inch thick.（约半英寸）。句式照搬、数字却由 quarter 偷改成 half，是最
阴的数字陷阱——不逐位核对数字就会上当。
借用原文：only about a quarter of an inch thick
D) 偷换概念
录音说板子强到能 stand up to heavy highway traffic（承受重型公路交通），D 却说
stand the wear and tear of natural elements.（耐受自然环境的磨损）。stand 这个动词
录音念过，但承受的对象从"重型交通"被偷换成"自然环境磨损"，后者原文没提。
借用原文：strong enough to stand up to heavy highway traffic

questions.stem: What has made it difficult to survey lions in remote parts of Sudan and Ethiopia?
options: A) The lack of clues about the species.
C) Endless fighting in the region.
D) The hazards from the desert.

explain.定位:
Continuous fighting in the region has made surveys difficult.
该地区持续不断的战乱使得调查工作变得困难。
explain.信号:
made … difficult 因果信号。定位靠的是因果障碍信号：录音里 has made surveys
difficult 这一短语正对应题干的 made it difficult to survey，它前面的主语 Continuous
fighting in the region 就是造成困难的原因。听到 made … difficult 就该立刻锁定它前面
的主语。
explain.替换:
Continuous fighting in the region ↔ Endless fighting in the region
Continuous=Endless 近义替换
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
录音确实提到此前 no one presented convincing evidence（无人拿出有力证据），听起
来像『缺线索』，但那是讲『过去为何没定论』，并非题干问的『让调查变难』的原因。把
它当 A 选，是被『缺证据』的语义带偏，答非所问。
借用原文：no one presented convincing evidence
B) 未提及
Inadequate funding for research. 说『研究缺钱』，但全文只说研究 supported by a
charity organization（有慈善机构资助），从没说经费不足。这是凭常识『科研常缺钱』
脑补出来的，录音里没有依据。
D) 未提及
The hazards from the desert. 说困难来自沙漠的危险。录音讲的是在国家公园露营、布相
机，全程没提沙漠或其危险；这是借『非洲、野外』的背景联想硬造出的障碍，原文没有。

questions.stem: What was the main purpose of the research?
options: A) To observe the wildlife in the two national parks.
B) To study the habitat of lions in Sudan and Ethiopia.
C) To identify the reasons for the lions' disappearance.
D) To find evidence of the existence of the "lost lions".

explain.定位:
But scientists released a report Monday documenting with hard evidence the discovery of
"lost lions."
但是科学家们周一发布了一份报告，用确凿的证据记录下了对"消失的狮子"的发现。
explain.信号:
转折but后才是真意。定位靠转折信号：But scientists released a report 的 But 把前文
『狮子在非洲大片消失、调查困难』的铺垫一转，转折之后才是这则新闻的核心——用确凿
证据 documenting with hard evidence the discovery of "lost lions"，即研究就是为了
证明这些消失的狮子还在。
explain.替换:
documenting with hard evidence the discovery of "lost lions" ↔
To find evidence of the existence of the "lost lions"
拿证据记录发现=找存在证据
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
To observe the wildlife in the two national parks. 借用了录音里的 national park 制造熟
耳感，但研究目的不是泛泛地『观察野生动物』，而是专门找狮子还在的证据。把发生地点
national park 当成目的，是听到原词就想选。
借用原文：camping in a national park
B) 原词陷阱
To study the habitat of lions in Sudan and Ethiopia. 把录音里的地名 Sudan and
Ethiopia 搬进选项，听着很熟。但研究目的是『证明狮子还在』，不是研究其栖息地
（habitat 录音根本没提）。属盗用地名+脑补 habitat。
借用原文：Sudan and Ethiopia
C) 与原文相反
To identify the reasons for the lions' disappearance. 说目的是『查清狮子消失的原
因』。录音只说狮子曾 disappeared from much of Africa，研究做的是证明它们还在、而
非研究为何消失，方向正好相反。
借用原文：Lions have disappeared from much of Africa

questions.stem: What did the researchers find in the national park?
options: D) Traps set by local hunters.

explain.定位:
The researchers set out six camera traps, capturing images of lions, and the identified
lion tracks.
研究者们布设了六台相机陷阱（红外相机），拍到了狮子的影像，并辨认出了狮子的足迹。
explain.信号:
identified 发现动词信号。定位靠发现动词：identified lion tracks 里的 identified（辨
认出）正是『发现』动作，紧跟其后的宾语 lion tracks 就是研究者找到的东西，直接对应
选项。
explain.替换:
identified lion tracks ↔ Lions' tracks
lion tracks=Lions' tracks 几近原词
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
Lions walking. 借了录音 capturing images of lions（拍到狮子的影像）里的 lions 制造熟
耳感，但录音只说拍到狮子的『影像』，从没说拍到『狮子在走动』walking 这个动作，是
把影像脑补成了具体动作。
借用原文：capturing images of lions
C) 原词陷阱
Some camping facilities. 借用录音里的 camping in a national park 的 camping 制造熟
耳感。但 camping 说的是研究者在公园里露营两晚这件事，不是他们『发现』了某些露营
设施，张冠李戴。
借用原文：camping in a national park
D) 原词陷阱
Traps set by local hunters. 是最毒的一项：它盗用了录音 set out six camera traps 里的
traps。但录音的 traps 是研究者布设的 camera traps（红外相机），不是『当地猎人设的
陷阱』；既换了设置人（研究者→hunters），又换了性质（相机→捕猎陷阱）。
借用原文：set out six camera traps

questions.stem: What is the woman looking forward to?
options: A) A special gift from the man.
C) A call from her dad.

explain.定位:
Oh, yes. That's right. This year would be my golden birthday.
哦，对，没错。今年是我的"黄金生日"。
explain.信号:
女士对男士提问的直接应答。男士先说 David told me you had a special birthday
coming up.，女士紧接着应答 This year would be my golden birthday.——被问者的直
接确认就是答案信号，她盼的正是这个特殊生日。
explain.替换:
my golden birthday ↔ Her 'lucky birthday'.
golden = lucky 同义改写
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项说她盼"男士送的特别礼物"，但录音里男士从头到尾没说要送礼，是凭空造出来的对
象。
B) 偷换概念
录音反复讲的是 golden birthday（生日），选项却换成 wedding anniversary（结婚纪念
日）；二者都和"重要日子"沾边，易混，但录音从未提纪念日。
借用原文：my golden birthday
C) 原词陷阱
录音第6段提到女士 my parents（父母），选项把它扭成"爸爸来电"——它蹭了"家人"这个
原词印象，但女士盼的是生日，不是一通电话，听到"父母"就选 C 正中圈套。
借用原文：my parents

questions.stem: What did the woman's parents do on her sister's lucky birthday?
options: A) Threw her a surprise party.
B) Took her on a trip overseas.
C) Bought her a gold necklace.
D) Gave her a big model plane.

explain.定位:
Come to think of it, my parents did throw her a surprise party that year.
这么一想，那一年我父母确实给她办了个惊喜派对。
explain.信号:
出现题干限定词 parents + 动作动词。这句里同时出现题干锁定的 my parents 和动作
throw her a surprise party，主语、对象、动作三对齐，正是承载答案的那一句。
explain.替换:
throw her a surprise party ↔ Threw her a surprise party.
几乎原句对应，仅时态调整
explain.排除:
B) 张冠李戴
录音里"旅行"是后文 My husband is planning a surprise holiday 说的、是丈夫为女士本
人筹划的；选项却把"带旅行"安到父母为姐姐做的事上，主体和对象都错位了。
借用原文：My husband is planning a surprise holiday
C) 原词陷阱
本组话题是 golden birthday，选项 Bought her a gold necklace. 借 gold 一词制造"听到
gold 就想选"的诱惑，但录音从没说父母买金项链。
借用原文：A golden or lucky birthday
D) 未提及
Gave her a big model plane.【模型飞机】在录音里完全没出现，是凭空编造的实物，无
任何原文影子。

questions.stem: What is the woman eager to find out about?
options: A) What her husband and the man are up to.
B) What has been troubling her husband.
C) The trip her husband has planned.
D) The gift her husband has bought.

explain.定位:
Anything you'd like to share? I'm dying to know what kind of trip he has planned where
we're going.
有什么能透露给我的吗？我太想知道他计划的是什么样的旅行、我们要去哪儿了。
explain.信号:
强烈愿望信号 I'm dying to know。I'm dying to know what kind of trip he has
planned 里 dying to know 是"急切想知道"的强信号，正对应题干 eager to find out，其
宾语 trip 就是她好奇的对象。
explain.替换:
what kind of trip he has planned ↔ The trip her husband has planned.
trip…he has planned 同义对应
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
选项说她想知道"丈夫和男士在搞什么"，但女士追问的只是丈夫计划的旅行 what kind of
trip he has planned，并没把男士也算进她好奇的对象里——选项擅自多绑一个人。
借用原文：what kind of trip he has planned
B) 答非所问
"想知道假期结果如何"是结尾男士说的 I can't wait to hear all about it when you get
back.，不是女士此刻好奇的；女士好奇的是出发前的"旅行计划"，不是回来后的"结果"。
借用原文：I can't wait to hear all about it when you get back.
D) 偷换概念
The gift her husband has bought. 与正解 The trip her husband has planned. 仅一词之
差，把"旅行"换成"礼物"；录音明说她想知道的是 what kind of trip，是 trip 不是 gift。
借用原文：what kind of trip he has planned

questions.stem: What does the man say at the end of the conversation?
options: A) He wants to find out about the couple's holiday plan.
B) He is eager to learn how the couple's holiday turns out.
C) He will tell the woman the secret if her husband agrees.
D) He will be glad to be a guide for the couple's holiday trip.

explain.定位:
I'm sure both of you will have a fantastic time. Happy golden birthday! I can't wait to hear all
about it when you get back.
我相信你俩会玩得超开心。生日快乐！我都等不及你们回来后听你讲这一路的事了。
explain.信号:
对话收尾句 + 强愿望词 can't wait。这是男士在对话末尾的发言，I can't wait to hear all
about it when you get back. 用 can't wait 表达"急切想听"，when you get back 点明
是"回来后听结果"——结尾位置 + 强愿望信号双重确认这是答案句。
explain.替换:
I can't wait to hear all about it when you get back ↔
He is eager to learn how the couple's holiday turns out.
can't wait to hear=eager to learn；回来后听=结果如何
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
选项说他"想搞清楚旅行计划"，但男士说的是 when you get back（回来后听），是事后的
结果，不是事前的计划；而且想打听计划的恰恰是女士不是男士，方向反了。
借用原文：I can't wait to hear all about it when you get back.
C) 未提及
He will tell the woman the secret if her husband agrees. 说他"若丈夫同意就告诉她秘
密"，但男士全程在装糊涂（Yeah, nothing at all.），从未做这种带条件的承诺。
D) 过度推断
He will be glad to be a guide for the couple's holiday trip. 说他乐意当向导，但男士只
表达了祝福与想听结果，根本没说要陪同/带路，是凭祝福硬推出来的。
借用原文：I'm sure both of you will have a fantastic time.

questions.stem: What does the man say about good negotiators?
options: A) They take the rival's attitude into account.
B) They know when to adopt a tough attitude.
C) They see the importance of making compromises.
D) They are sensitive to the dynamics of a negotiation.

explain.定位:
They are sensitive to the dynamics in the negotiation. The way it raises and falls, and how it
may change direction.
他们对谈判中的态势变化很敏感——它如何起伏，又如何可能改变方向。
explain.信号:
被问者一连串列举里的一条。男士在回答"什么样的人是成功谈判者"时连说好几条特征，
They are sensitive to the dynamics in the negotiation. 是其中一条，与选项 D 几乎对

They are sensitive to the dynamics of a negotiation.

explain.排除:

They see the importance of making compromises. 里的 compromises 确实在录音里出

评点"好谈判者特征"时说的，属把别处原词搬来答非所问的原词陷阱。

they know when to stop ↔ They know when to stop.
原句照搬，几乎零改写
explain.排除:
B)
They know how to adapt. 与录音 They are firm, but flexible. 的"灵活"沾边，但录音并未

questions.stem: What do some people want to know about space exploration?
options: A) How space research benefits people on Earth.

他们想知道太空研究如何造福地球上的人们。

want to know 与原文 want to know 信号对上，这句就是答案句。

how space research helps people on Earth ↔ How space research benefits people on Earth

options: A) They tried to make best use of the latest technology.
B) They tried to meet astronauts' specific requirements.
C) They developed objects for astronauts to use in outer space.

In early space programs, such as the Apollo missions of the 1960s and 1970s, and in the space

中，科学家们研制了供宇航员在月球上和太空中使用的物品。

题干 space shuttle missions 在原文同句出现，紧跟 scientists 的动作。录音里 in the
space shuttle missions today, scientists developed objects for the astronauts to use
on the moon and in space 既含题干的定位词 space shuttle missions，又紧跟
scientists developed… 这一动作——定位词 + 主语动作同现，这句就是答案句。
explain.替换:
scientists developed objects for the astronauts to use on the moon and in space ↔
They developed objects for astronauts to use in outer space

in colonial America in Yankee New England where one of my ancestors lived, because it was
the beginning of something.

扬基地区的殖民地美洲，因为那是某种开端。

I would have enjoyed spending my evenings in that environment, discussing new

小椅子上做针线活。

options: A) Sit down and try to calm yourself.
B) Call your family or friends for help.
C) Use a map to identify your location.
D) Try to follow your footprints back.

questions.stem: What will happen if you follow an unknown stream in the woods?

C) You may expose yourself to unexpected dangers.

强调「有危险」的基调完全相反，纯属凑数。

从没说过的具体后果，听到 stream、river 就选它会中招。

walk uphill ↔ Walk uphill.
动作短语原样对应

Look for food. 借录音 there are more eatable plants（有更多可吃植物）勾起「找吃

questions.stem: Elderly students find it hard to keep up with the rapid changes in education.
questions.passage:
Do In-Class Exams Make Students Study Harder?

Research suggests they may study more broadly for the unexpected rather than search for answers.

A) I have always been a poor test-taker. So it may seem rather strange that I have returned to college to finish the degree I left undone some four decades ago. I am making my way through Columbia University, surrounded by students who quickly supply the verbal answer while I am still processing the question.

B) Since there is no way for me to avoid exams, I am currently questioning what kind of exams are the most taxing and ultimately beneficial. I have already sweated through numerous in-class midterms and finals, and now I have a professor who issues take-home ones. I was excited when I learned this, figuring I had a full week to do the research, read the texts, and write it all up. In fact, I was still rewriting my midterm the morning it was due. To say I had lost the thread is putting it mildly.

C) As I was suffering through my week of anxiety, overthinking the material and guessing my grasp of it, I did some of my own polling among students and professors. David Eisenbach, who teaches a popular class on U.S. presidents at Columbia, prefers the in-class variety. He believes students ultimately learn more and encourages them to form study groups. "That way they socialize over history outside the class, which wouldn't happen without the pressure of an in-class exam," he explained, "Furthermore, in-class exams force students to learn how to perform under pressure, an essential work skill."

D) He also says there is less chance of cheating with the in-class variety. In 2012, 125 students at Harvard were caught up in a scandal when it was discovered they had cheated on a take-home exam for a class entitled "Introduction To Congress." Some colleges have what they call an "honor code," though if you are smart enough to get into these schools, you are either smart enough to get around any codes or hopefully, too ethical to consider doing so. As I sat blocked and clueless for two solid days, I momentarily wondered if I couldn't just call an expert on the subject matter which I was tackling, or someone who took the class previously, to get me going.

E) Following the Harvard scandal, Mary Miller, the former dean of students at Yale, made an impassioned appeal to her school's professors to refrain from take-home exams. "Students risk health and well being, as well as performance in other end-of-term work, when faculty offers take-home exams without clear, time-limited boundaries," she told me. "Research now shows that regular quizzes, short essays, and other assignments over the course of a term better enhance learning and retention."

F) Most college professors agree the kind of exam they choose largely depends on the subject. A quantitative-based one, for example, is unlikely to be sent home, where one could ask their older brothers and sisters to help. Vocational-type classes, such as computer science or journalism, on the other hand, are often more research-oriented and lend themselves to take-home testing. Chris Koch, who teaches "History of Broadcast Journalism" at Montgomery Community College in Rockville, Maryland, points out that reporting is about investigation rather than the memorization of minute details. "In my field, it's not what you know—it's what you know how to find out," says Koch. "There is way too much information, and more coming all the time, for anyone to remember. I want my students to search out the answers to questions by using all the resources available to them."

G) Students' test-form preferences vary, too, often depending on the subject and course difficulty. "I prefer take-home essays because it is then really about the writing, so you have time to edit and do more research," says Elizabeth Dresser, a junior at Barnard. Then there is the stress factor. Francesca Haass, a senior at Middlebury, says, "I find the in-class ones are more stressful in the short term, but there is immediate relief as you swallow information like mad, and then you get to forget it all. Take-homes require thoughtful engagement which can lead to longer term stress as there is never a moment when the time is up." Meanwhile, Olivia Rubin, a sophomore at Emory, says she hardly even considers take-homes true exams. "If you understand the material and have the ability to articulate(说出) your thoughts, they should be a breeze."

H) How students ultimately handle tests may depend on their personal test-taking abilities. There are people who always wait until the last minute, and make it much harder than it needs to be. And then there are those who, not knowing what questions are coming at them, and having no resources to refer to, can freeze. And then there are we rare folks who fit both those descriptions.

I) Yes, my advanced age must factor into the equation(等式), in part because of my inability to access the information as quickly. As another returning student at Columbia, Kate Marber, told me, "We are learning not only all this information, but essentially how to learn again. Our fellow students have just come out of high school. A lot has changed since we were last in school."

J) If nothing else, the situation has given my college son and me something to share. When I asked his opinion on this matter, "I like in-class exams because the time is already reserved, as opposed to using my free time at home to work on a test," he responded. It seems to me that a compromise would be receiving the exam questions a day or two in advance, and then doing the actual test in class with the ticking clock overhead.

K) Better yet, how about what one Hunter College professor reportedly did recently for her final exam: She encouraged the class not to stress or even study, promising that, "It is going to be a piece of cake." When the students came in, sharpened pencils in hand, there was not a bluebook in sight. Rather, they saw a large chocolate cake and they each were given a slice.

questions.stem: What did researchers find puzzling about the first-night effect?
options: A) To what extent it can trouble people.
B) What role it has played in evolution.
C) What circumstances may trigger it.
D) In what way it can be beneficial.
questions.passage:
That people often experience trouble sleeping in a different bed in unfamiliar surroundings is a phenomenon known as the "first-night" effect. If a person stays in the same room the following night they tend to sleep more soundly. Yuka Sasaki and her colleagues at Brown University set out to investigate the origins of this effect.

Dr. Sasaki knew the first-night effect probably has something to do with how humans evolved. The puzzle was what benefit would be gained from it when performance might be affected the following day. She also knew from previous work conducted on birds and dolphins that these animals put half of their brains to sleep at a time so that they can rest while remaining alert enough to avoid predators(捕食者). This led her to wonder if people might be doing the same thing. To take a closer look, her team studied 35 healthy people as they slept in the unfamiliar environment of the university's Department of Psychological Sciences. The participants each slept in the department for two nights and were carefully monitored with techniques that looked at the activity of their brains. Dr. Sasaki found, as expected, the participants slept less well on their first night than they did on their second, taking more than twice as long to fall asleep and sleeping less overall. During deep sleep, the participants' brains behaved in a similar manner seen in birds and dolphins. On the first night only, the left hemispheres(半球) of their brains did not sleep nearly as deeply as their right hemispheres did.

Curious if the left hemispheres were indeed remaining awake to process information detected in the surrounding environment, Dr. Sasaki re-ran the experiment while presenting the sleeping participants with a mix of regularly timed beeps(蜂鸣声) of the same tone and irregular beeps of a different tone during the night. She worked out that, if the left hemisphere was staying alert to keep guard in a strange environment, then it would react to the irregular beeps by stirring people from sleep and would ignore the regularly timed ones. This is precisely what she found.

questions.stem: What does the author say is the problem with women?
options: A) They are often unclear about the career goals to reach.
B) They are usually more committed at home than on the job.
C) They tend to be over-optimistic about how far they could go.
D) They tend to push themselves beyond the limits of their ability.
questions.passage:
It's time to reevaluate how women handle conflict at work. Being overworked or over-committed at home and on the job will not get you where you want to be in life. It will only slow you down and hinder your career goals.

Did you know women are more likely than men to feel exhausted? Nearly twice as many women than men ages 18-44 reported feeling "very tired" or "exhausted", according to a recent study.

This may not be surprising given that this is the age range when women have children. It's also the age range when many women are trying to balance careers and home. One reason women may feel exhausted is that they have a hard time saying "no." Women want to be able to do it all—volunteer for school parties or cook delicious meals—and so their answer to any request is often "Yes, I can."

Women struggle to say "no" in the workplace for similar reasons, including the desire to be liked by their colleagues. Unfortunately, this inability to say "no" may be hurting women's health as well as their career.

At the workplace, men use conflict as a way to position themselves, while women often avoid conflict or strive to be the peacemaker, because they don't want to be viewed as aggressive or disruptive at work. For example, there's a problem that needs to be addressed immediately, resulting in a dispute over who should be the one to fix it. Men are more likely to face that dispute from the perspective of what benefits them most, whereas women may approach the same dispute from the perspective of what's the easiest and quickest way to resolve the problem—even if that means doing the boring work themselves.

This difference in handling conflict could be the deciding factor on who gets promoted to a leadership position and who does not. Leaders have to be able to delegate and manage resources wisely – including staff expertise. Shouldering more of the workload may not earn you that promotion. Instead, it may highlight your inability to delegate effectively.
